work: Hesiod, the Homeric Hymns, and Homerica

items.name: the lyre of Hermes
items.description: Seven-stringed lyre Hermes makes from a tortoise shell, then gives to Apollo in exchange for the herds.

items.name: the wooden horse
items.description: Hollow horse the Greeks build; the Trojans bring it inside Ilium, leading to the city's sack.

wikipedia.lead: In Greek mythology, the Trojan Horse was a wooden horse said to have been used by the Greeks during the Trojan War to sneak into the city of Troy and win the war. The Trojan Horse is not mentioned in Homer's Iliad, with the poem ending before the war is concluded, and it is only briefly mentioned in the Odyssey.

items.name: the swaddled stone
items.description: Stone wrapped as a child, swallowed by Cronos in place of Zeus and later set at Pytho.

wikipedia.lead: An omphalos is a religious stone artefact. In Ancient Greek, the word ὀμφᾰλός means "navel".

items.name: the shield of Heracles
items.description: Unbreakable shield adorned with Fear, Strife, snakes and scenes of war and peace, carried against Cycnus and Ares.

wikipedia.lead: The Shield of Heracles is an archaic Greek epic poem that was attributed to Hesiod during antiquity. The subject of the poem is the expedition of Heracles and Iolaus against Cycnus, the son of Ares, who challenged Heracles to combat as Heracles was passing through Thessaly.

items.name: Hesiod's tripod
items.description: Prize Hesiod wins at the games of Amphidamas at Chalcis and dedicates to the Muses.

items.name: Zeus' thunderbolt
items.description: Weapon given to Zeus by his freed uncles, used against the Titans, Typhoeus and Asclepius.

wikipedia.lead: A thunderbolt, or lightning bolt, is a symbolic representation of lightning. It appears variously in history, literature, and in contemporary warnings of (typically high-voltage) electricity.

items.name: Arion
items.description: Swift horse Heracles drives against Ares; also Adrastus' horse in flight from Thebes.

wikipedia.lead: In Greek mythology, Arion or Areion, is a divinely-bred, fabulously fast, black-maned horse. He saved the life of Adrastus, king of Argos, during the war of the Seven against Thebes.

items.name: the Palladium
items.description: Sacred image of Athena at Troy, which Odysseus takes from Ilium before the horse is brought in.

wikipedia.lead: A palladium or palladion (plural palladia) is an image or other object of great antiquity on which the safety of a city or nation is said to depend. The word is a generalization from the name of the original Trojan Palladium, a wooden statue (xoanon) of Pallas Athena that Odysseus and Diomedes stole from the citadel of Troy.

items.name: the golden apples
items.description: Golden apples guarded by a snake; also used by Hippomenes to beat Atalanta in the race.

wikipedia.lead: The golden apple is an element that appears in various legends that depict a hero retrieving the golden apples hidden or stolen by an antagonist. Gold apples also appear on the Silver Branch of the Otherworld in Irish mythology.

items.name: the pomegranate seed
items.description: Seed Hades gives Persephone, binding her to spend part of each year below.

items.name: the Argo
items.description: Ship of the Argonauts, from which Heracles is left behind in Magnesia.

wikipedia.lead: In Greek mythology, the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts. The ship was built with divine aid and carried the Argonauts on their quest for the Golden Fleece from Iolcos to Colchis.

items.name: the golden fleece
items.description: Fleece of the ram of Phrixus, brought to Aeetes in Colchis.

wikipedia.lead: In Greek mythology, the Golden Fleece is the fleece of the golden-woolled, winged ram, Chrysomallos, which rescued Phrixus and brought him to Colchis, where Phrixus then sacrificed it to Zeus. Phrixus gave the fleece to King Aeëtes, who kept it in a sacred grove, whence Jason and the Argonauts stole it with the help of Medea, Aeëtes's daughter.

items.name: the golden necklace of Europa
items.description: Necklace Zeus gives Europa when he carries her to Crete.

items.name: the sickle
items.description: Sickle made by Earth, with which Cronos castrates his father Heaven.

items.name: Apollo's laurel rod
items.description: Laurel staff the Muses give Hesiod when they inspire him with song.

items.name: Pandora's jar
items.description: The jar Pandora opens, releasing evils among men while Hope stays inside.

wikipedia.lead: Pandora's box is an artefact in Greek mythology connected with the myth of Pandora in Hesiod's c. 700 B.C. poem Works and Days.

items.name: the Cretan ship
items.description: Ship bound for Pylos that Apollo boards as a dolphin, steering it to Crisa.

items.name: the cap of Hades
items.description: Cap that Perseus wears on the shield as he flees the Gorgons.

wikipedia.lead: In classical mythology, the Cap of Invisibility is a helmet or cap that can turn the wearer invisible, also known as the Cap of Hades or Helm of Hades.
